title: LRU Cache
summary: Build a fixed-capacity least-recently-used cache with O(1) operations.

stages.title: LRU cache
stages.requirement:
Implement `LRUCache(capacity)` (`capacity >= 1`):

- `get(key)` returns the value, or `None` if absent. A hit makes the key **most recently used**.
- `put(key, value)` inserts or updates the key and makes it most recently used. If inserting a
  **new** key would exceed the capacity, first evict the **least recently used** key.
- `len(cache)` returns the number of stored keys.

Values can be anything, including `None`.

```python
c = LRUCache(2)
c.put("a", 1); c.put("b", 2)
c.get("a")      # -> 1   ("a" is now most recent)
c.put("c", 3)   # evicts "b"
c.get("b")      # -> None
```

All operations must be O(1). Tests make 200,000 operations.

visibleTests.name: test_example
visibleTests.code:
def test_example():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    c.put("a", 1)
    c.put("b", 2)
    assert c.get("a") == 1
    c.put("c", 3)
    assert c.get("b") is None
    assert c.get("c") == 3

hiddenTests.name: test_update_refreshes_recency
hiddenTests.code:
def test_update_refreshes_recency():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    c.put("a", 1)
    c.put("b", 2)
    c.put("a", 10)
    c.put("c", 3)
    assert c.get("a") == 10
    assert c.get("b") is None

hiddenTests.name: test_update_does_not_evict
hiddenTests.code:
def test_update_does_not_evict():
    c = LRUCache(1)
    c.put("a", 1)
    c.put("a", 2)
    assert c.get("a") == 2
    assert len(c) == 1

hiddenTests.name: test_miss_does_not_change_order
hiddenTests.code:
def test_miss_does_not_change_order():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    c.put("a", 1)
    c.put("b", 2)
    assert c.get("zzz") is None
    c.put("c", 3)
    assert c.get("a") is None

hiddenTests.name: test_len
test_many_operations
hiddenTests.code:
def test_many_operations():
    c = LRUCache(1000)
    for i in range(100_000):
        c.put(i, i)
        c.get(i - 500)
    assert len(c) == 1000
    assert c.get(99_999) == 99_999
    assert c.get(98_000) is None

hints: You need O(1) lookup by key and O(1) "move to most recent" / "remove least recent".
A hash map plus a doubly linked list does both. In Python, `collections.OrderedDict` is exactly that: `move_to_end` and `popitem(last=False)`.
Interviewers often ask for the linked list by hand. Use sentinel head and tail nodes to avoid edge cases.

solution.explanation:
`OrderedDict` is a hash map threaded with a doubly linked list. `move_to_end` marks a key
as most recent and `popitem(last=False)` evicts the least recent, both in O(1). Note
that updating an existing key must not evict. In an interview, be ready to write the
node-based version with sentinel nodes, which is what `OrderedDict` does internally.
